oliver: Quick heads-up — noticed a 2x increase in client ack latency for streaming sessions last night when KV hit rate dipped under ~60%. p95 client->server ack went from ~40ms -> ~120ms. Anyone else seeing this?
marta: Yup, I saw a matching blip on token_latency_breakdown. Server-side token assembly stayed ~25ms but the client-ack bucket jumped hard. Could be waiting on something upstream (KV?). :thinking:
sam: I pulled a quick profile for one of the affected flows. perf-bot job ran on the canary cluster — link: https://perf.internal/jobs/1847654000 (contains traces). Kernel selection looked stable, batching heuristics didn't change, but KV miss rate spiked.
perf-bot: job 1847654000 complete — summary:
```
span: total_token_time_ms: p50=22 p95=38 p99=85
kv: hits=43% misses=57% (window=5m)
client_ack_wait_ms: p50=12 p95=118 p99=210
batcher_wait_ms: p50=6 p95=14 p99=40
notes: elevated client_ack correlated with kv miss bursts
```
kai: Hypothesis: dynamic_batcher is holding messages until KV lookups return for prefix cache warmup. If batching waits for KV, client ack will include KV latency. We should add an explicit metric where batcher records time spent blocked on KV (e.g., `batcher.kv_block_ms`) and a boolean tag `kv_blocked=true/false`.
anika: Also want to rule out kernel/path change — could fallback kernel cause higher overhead during misses? From the profile it didn't look like kernel churn, but add a flag in traces for `kernel_variant` so we can correlate.
oliver: Repro snippet I used (simulates low KV hit rate):
`curl -N -H \"X-Test-KV:low-hit\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream?model=rw_long`
You can see chunk stream fine but client ack delta increases by ~80-100ms. I also captured client-side timings in the header `X-Client-Ack-Ms`.
sam: For instrumentation: add `stream.client_ack_ms` at ingress, and `stream.server_ack_ms` before flush. Then a derived metric `stream.client_vs_server_ack_gap_ms`. Dashboards can show that split and per-route KPIs.
marta: I'll add a panel to the per-route dashboard: stacked p95s for client_ack, server_ack, kv_block_ms. Also add a heatmap for routes where client_vs_server_ack_gap > 50ms.
kai: Small tracing points to insert (pseudo):
```
batcher.enqueue(req)
  -> record('enqueue_ts')
  -> if waiting_for_kv: record('kv_wait_start')
kv.lookup(...)
  -> record('kv_wait_end')
batcher.flush()
  -> record('flush_ts')
```
Then create derived spans `kv_wait_ms = kv_wait_end - kv_wait_start` and tag on the batch span.
anika: I'll instrument kernel_variant and batch_policy in the trace root. That will let us pivot by kernel selection on the dashboard.
perf-bot: quick snapshot from current canary metrics (5m window):
```
route:/v1/stream p95_client_ack=118ms p95_server_ack=22ms kv_hit%=46% requests=12.1k
route:/v1/stream?model=rw_fast p95_client_ack=45ms p95_server_ack=20ms kv_hit%=82% requests=8.4k
```
sam: Good to have per-route comparison. If a route with low kv_hit% also shows high client_ack but stable server_ack then it's almost certainly KV contention/latency leaking to clients.
oliver: Action items:
- marta: add dashboard panels + heatmap (per-route p95s)
- sam: add server/client ack metrics and derived gap metric
- kai: instrument batcher kv wait and tag traces
- anika: kernel_variant + batch_policy on trace root
- ops: pin a short canary with simulated low-KV workload and run for 30m
marta: I'll open a quick PR for the dashboard (WIP) and drop screenshots here when ready. :+1:
deploy-bot: Canary for branch `stream-kv-instrumentation` deployed to canary-cluster at 2026-03-17T22:05:00Z — monitoring enabled.
oliver: Great — once metrics are in we can see whether batching heuristics or KV behavior is the main culprit. If it's KV we can consider local prefetch or async-ack heuristics to decouple client acks from KV resolution.
sam: Also consider a short-term fallback: when kv_hit_rate < 60% for a route, temporarily enable `ack_async=true` to avoid blocking clients. Add as a rollout knob in the console.
anika: Noted. I'll add kernel correlation panels too.
marta: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/dashboards/pull/617 — contains panel defs and alerts for client_vs_server_ack_gap > 100ms.
oliver: Thanks all. Let's regroup after the 30m canary run. :wave:
